problem:
Let $V=C[-1,1]$ be the vector space of all functions that are continuous on $[-1,1],$ equipped with the inner product 

$$
⟨f(t),g(t)⟩={\int }_{-1}^{1}f(t)g(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

Given the functions $f(t)=t$ and $g(t)=\operatorname{cos}⁡t,$ which of the following statements are true?

- $⟨f(t),g(t)⟩=0$
- $⟨f(t),g(t)⟩=\pi $
- $f(t)⊥g(t)$ with respect to the inner product $⟨\cdot ,\cdot ⟩$ in $V$
worked_solution:
First, we need to evaluate 

$$
⟨f(t),g(t)⟩={\int }_{-1}^{1}t\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,\text{d}t.
$$

Let's use integration by parts. We denote

$$
\begin{aligned}u=t & ⟹ & {u}^{′}=1, \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{cos}⁡t & ⟹ & v=\int {v}^{′}\,\text{d}t=\int \operatorname{cos}⁡t\,\text{d}t=\operatorname{sin}⁡t.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, applying the integration by parts formula, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-1}^{1}t\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,\text{d}t & =uv{|}_{-1}^{1}-{\int }_{-1}^{1}{u}^{′}v\,\text{d}t \\  & =(t\operatorname{sin}⁡t){|}_{-1}^{1}-{\int }_{-1}^{1}\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,\text{d}t \\  & =(1\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(1)-(-1)\operatorname{sin}⁡(-1))-\operatorname{cos}⁡t{|}_{-1}^{1} \\  & =(\operatorname{sin}⁡(1)+\operatorname{sin}⁡(-1))+(\operatorname{cos}⁡(1)-\operatorname{cos}⁡(-1)) \\  & =(\operatorname{sin}⁡(1)-\operatorname{sin}⁡(1))+(\operatorname{cos}⁡(1)-\operatorname{cos}⁡(1)) \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Let's now examine the statements:

- Statement I is true, while statement II is false. This is as a result of the above calculations.

- Statement III is true. Since the inner product is zero, our vectors must be orthogonal.

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and III only."
